source.title: Updated Manufactured Cost Analysis for Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolyzers
source.basis: Table 1 (printed page 5, PDF page 18), Figure 3 (printed page 6), section 3 (printed page 28). Table and figures visually checked. Future loading case: Table A-7 (printed page 65, PDF page 78); section 3.5 and Figure 25 (printed pages 45-50) treat this as an isolated theoretical change. Table visually checked.

projection.basis: NREL 87625 Table A-7 very-low-PGM loading case; Figure 25 applies isolated changes individually. Use its paired loadings without combining the separate high-current-density case.
projection.calendar_assumption: The source does not date achievement. Assign 2050 as an explicit scenario assumption, not a published prediction. Hold the 2022 baseline for the 2020 backcast; interpolate linearly from 2022 to 2050.
projection.operating_point: Retain 2 A/cm2 and 1.9 V/cell throughout. No current-density, efficiency, nominal-capacity or hydrogen-productivity improvement is credited by this catalyst-only scenario.
projection.durability: Retain source nominal 45000-hour stack life and replacement-inclusive four-stack lifetime allocation. This is an explicit unchanged-durability assumption, not a validated outcome at lower loading. NREL warns of performance and durability trade-offs.
projection.sensitivity: fixed-baseline retains 2 mg Ir/cm2 and 1 mg Pt/cm2 at all supported years; all other inputs and the support endpoints are identical.
projection.uncertainty: Scenario assumptions, not measured future observations. Deterministic paired design points; do not independently sample metal bounds.

application.temporal_policy: Default prospective case: hold the 2022 baseline in 2020-2022, then linearly reduce both loadings to the paired NREL Table A-7 case by assumed 2050. Source does not assign that date. Preserve source outside 2020-2050. A fixed-baseline sensitivity is available offline.
application.uncertainty: Deterministic paired scenario with explicit loading and unchanged-durability assumptions. Identical bounds do not imply zero engineering uncertainty.

citation_audit.workbook_reference_title: Life cycle assessment of an alkaline fuel cell CHP system
citation_audit.status: Mismatch verified; true numerical source unresolved. Its catalyst observations are not used by this replacement. Original historical workbook preserved. Potassium and titanium observations remain separate source-review issues.

limits: Matched active-electrode catalyst reference, not a complete reconstruction or validation of all stack hardware and manufacturing.
Ruthenium zero belongs to this pure-Ir anode/Pt cathode design. It does not assert that all PEM catalysts lack Ru.
Source loadings are contained PGM metal, not oxide mass. MW scaling uses cell terminal DC power; system AC power and delivered hydrogen energy are different boundaries.
Exact 1 MW area is used. Source rounded geometry produces 999780 W, a 0.022% difference. Cell count is not multiplied into the already summed area again.

PTL and bipolar plate platinum coatings are additional to cathode catalyst; their complete quantity is unresolved and is not claimed included in the catalyst-only Pt input. Source mentions 0.1 micrometre PTL coating but complete face counts, coating areas/yields and bipolar-plate coating thickness need separate reconciliation.

Retained catalyst mass is represented with 100% incorporation at the direct refined-metal purchase boundary. Catalyst manufacturing losses, recovery, processing and electrode life are not independently validated; no factory-line cost yield is treated as a measured metal yield.

Existing non-catalyst materials, hydrogen-output/energy coefficients and 45000-hour nominal stack life with its replacement count are retained source proxies. The source is not asserted to match NREL complete system performance or lifetime.

The source hydrogen recipe uses 54 kWh/kg while the NREL reference separately reports 51.1 stack + 4.2 BOP kWh/kg. These are distinct model assumptions; the catalyst correction does not claim a jointly validated complete hydrogen-system design.

Future loading reduction follows a theoretical isolated NREL sensitivity assigned to 2050 by this scenario. It is not demonstrated joint performance, lifetime and commercial adoption. Fixed-baseline sensitivity is retained; hardware coatings remain separate.
No primary/secondary-share, refinery-allocation, throughput or accepted scenario-result changes are made by this authoring step.
